Title: Query-bag Matching with Mutual Coverage for Information-seeking Conversations in E-commerce
Query-bag Matching with Mutual Coverage for Information-seeking Conversations in E-commerce Zhenxin Fu∗ fuzhenxin@pku.edu.cn zhongxiu.jf@alibaba-inc.com WICT, Peking University DAMO Academy, Alibaba Group Wei Zhou Dongyan Zhao fayi.zw@alibaba-inc.com zhaodongyan@pku.edu.cn DAMO Academy, Alibaba Group WICT, Peking University arXiv:1911.02747v1 [cs.CL] 7 Nov 2019 ruiyan@pku.edu.cn WICT, Peking University ABSTRACT Information-seeking conversation system aims at satisfying the information needs of users through conversations.

[2] Source: 1911.02747.pdf | Page: 2 | Section: 1 INTRODUCTION
Title: Query-bag Matching with Mutual Coverage for Information-seeking Conversations in E-commerce
The ablation study shows the usefulness of the components. The contributions in this paper are summarized as follows: 1) To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to adopt query-bag matching in the information-seeking conversation. 2) We propose the mutual coverage model to measure the information coverage in the query-bag matching. 3) We release the composite Quora dataset to facilitate the research in this area.

[3] Source: 1911.02747.pdf | Page: 2 | Section: 2 METHODOLOGY
Title: Query-bag Matching with Mutual Coverage for Information-seeking Conversations in E-commerce
hCNN is a CNN based matching model which is fast enough to work on the industry application. The input of hCNN is a query q and the i-th question bi in the bag. q and bi are fed into a CNN respectively. A cross-attention matrix Mi is fed into another CNN to get the interaction representation between them. Each element of Mi is defined as Mi a,b = q⊤a · bi,b where qa is the word embedding of the a-th word in query q and bi,b is the embedding of the b-th word in bi.

[4] Source: 1911.02747.pdf | Page: 2 | Section: 1 INTRODUCTION
Title: Query-bag Matching with Mutual Coverage for Information-seeking Conversations in E-commerce
In this paper, we propose a simple but effective mutual coverage component to model the above-mentioned problem. The coverage is based on the cross-attention matrix of the query-bag pair which in- dicates the matching degree of elements between the query and bag. The mutual coverage is performed by stacking the cross-attention matrix along two directions, i.e., query and bag, in the word level respectively.

[5] Source: 1911.02747.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: None
Title: Query-bag Matching with Mutual Coverage for Information-seeking Conversations in E-commerce
Text matching between a user query and a pre-collected question is an important part of the information-seeking conversation in E-commerce. In the practical scenario, a sort of questions always correspond to a same answer. Naturally, these questions can form a bag. Learning the matching between user query and bag directly may improve the conversation performance, denoted as query-bag matching.

[6] Source: 1911.02747.pdf | Page: 4 | Section: 5 CONCLUSION
Title: Query-bag Matching with Mutual Coverage for Information-seeking Conversations in E-commerce
2017. Enhanced LSTM for Natural Language Inference. 1657–1668. [3] Hang Li and Jun Xu.

[7] Source: 1911.02747.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: 1 INTRODUCTION
Title: Query-bag Matching with Mutual Coverage for Information-seeking Conversations in E-commerce
When a user poses a query to the bot, the bot searches the most similar bag and uses the corresponding answer to reply to the user. The more information in the query covered by the bag, the more likely the bag’s corresponding answer answers the query. What’s more, the bag should not have too much information exceeding the query. Thus modelling the bag-to-query and query-to-bag coverage is essential in this task.

[8] Source: 1911.02747.pdf | Page: 4 | Section: 5 CONCLUSION
Title: Query-bag Matching with Mutual Coverage for Information-seeking Conversations in E-commerce
5 CONCLUSION In this paper, we propose the QBM model which performs the query- bag matching in information-seeking conversation. Experiments show that the proposed mutual coverage component improves the model performance. And the model can automatically discover im- portant words in the query or bag from both the coverage weighting component and the word-level bag representation.

[9] Source: 1911.02747.pdf | Page: 2 | Section: 1 INTRODUCTION
Title: Query-bag Matching with Mutual Coverage for Information-seeking Conversations in E-commerce
Figure 1: The proposed query-bag matching (QBM) model. The upper right is the query-bag coverage component (we only show the bag-to-query coverage in the Figure for demonstration, and the query-to-bag coverage is similar with bag-to-query coverage). q is the query, and bi is the i- th question in the bag. Mi is the cross-attention matrix be- tween q and bi. The bottom lines indicate the TF-IDF based bag representation construction. br is a new “question” for bag representation.

[10] Source: 1911.02747.pdf | Page: 3 | Section: 2 METHODOLOGY
Title: Query-bag Matching with Mutual Coverage for Information-seeking Conversations in E-commerce
The concatenation of {c1, . ,cn} across all questions in a bag forms the query-to-bag coverage vector cb. In addition, not all words in a question should be treated equally. The word “the” contributes little to the matching degree in most cases. However, “package” is very important in the E-commerce scenario.

[11] Source: 1911.02747.pdf | Page: 2 | Section: 1 INTRODUCTION
Title: Query-bag Matching with Mutual Coverage for Information-seeking Conversations in E-commerce
Our model obtains 0.05 and 0.03 R10@1 gains comparing to the strongest baseline in the two datasets.
